weakness: Engine holds an RLock across the full OPA evaluation: internal/policy/engine.go evaluates policies while holding the read lock over the policy set, so a concurrent CRD write (write-lock acquisition) can stall admission for the duration of an evaluation, coupling control-plane CRD churn to data-plane admission latency (availability).
remediation: Snapshot the policy slice under a brief lock then evaluate lock-free (release the RLock before calling OPA); writers swap the snapshot atomically. Add a concurrency test proving a CRD write does not block in-flight evaluations.
milestones: M1 Refactor to snapshot-then-eval-lock-free; M2 concurrency regression test; M3 verify admission p99 latency is decoupled from CRD write rate.

weakness: Decision-publisher drops events under backpressure with no spool: the webhook->policy-manager DecisionPublisher discards decision-telemetry events when its buffer is full and has no disk-spool, so under load the management-plane decision feed silently loses events. This is AU-2 telemetry (the dashboard decision feed), NOT the durable, HMAC-sealed audit log (which is the AU-9 system of record), but the silent drop is still a monitoring gap.
remediation: Confirm and document that the DecisionPublisher feed is telemetry-only (the durable audit log is independent and unaffected), and add/verify a Prometheus alert on the drop metric so backpressure is observable rather than silent. Spooling is out of scope if telemetry-only is confirmed.
milestones: M1 Confirm telemetry-only vs durable-record boundary in code + SSP; M2 alert on the publish-drop metric; M3 document the boundary in the audit-architecture narrative.

weakness: Audit LogConfigChange/LogSystemEvent synthesize correlation_id and request_id from time.Now().UnixNano(): two events generated within the same nanosecond tick (or on coarse-resolution clocks) can collide, undermining the uniqueness guarantee that AU-3/AU-12 correlation relies on for time-correlated trail reconstruction.
remediation: Generate correlation_id / request_id with a UUID (e.g. github.com/google/uuid) instead of UnixNano, guaranteeing uniqueness independent of clock resolution. Add a test asserting two events created in a tight loop have distinct IDs.
milestones: M1 Replace UnixNano ID synthesis with UUID; M2 uniqueness test; M3 verify downstream correlation/dedup logic still keys correctly.

weakness: require-image-digest rule uses a substring '@sha256:' check, not an anchored 64-hex digest: the opt-in require-digest policy rule matches any reference containing the literal '@sha256:' substring, so a crafted/malformed reference (e.g. trailing or short hex) can pass the digest-pinning check without being a valid 64-hex sha256 digest (CM-6, opt-in rule).
remediation: Replace the substring check with an anchored regular expression requiring @sha256: followed by exactly 64 lowercase hex characters at end of reference. Add positive/negative fixtures (valid digest passes; short/long/non-hex rejected).
milestones: M1 Anchored 64-hex regex; M2 positive/negative rule fixtures; M3 golden-test the rule in the policy suite.

weakness: Audit redaction key-substring allow-list misses common credential key names: the redaction pass keys off a substring list that omits authorization, access_key, connection, dsn, webhook, sas, jwt, and pem, so audit records can persist these credential-bearing fields in cleartext before the HMAC seal (AU-3(1) over-collection / SC-28 at-rest exposure).
remediation: Expand the redaction key-substring list to include authorization/access_key/connection/dsn/webhook/sas/jwt/pem (and review for further common credential key names). Add a test asserting each new key is redacted before seal.
milestones: M1 Expand redaction key list; M2 per-key redaction test; M3 review record schema for other credential-bearing fields.

weakness: forward-auth mode trusts client-supplied X-Forwarded-Access-Token / X-Forwarded-User headers with no in-binary guard: when the management plane runs behind an auth proxy in forward-auth mode, it consumes identity headers without verifying it is actually behind a trusted proxy, so a direct caller (absent a NetworkPolicy boundary) can spoof identity by setting those headers (IA-2/AC-3).
remediation: Add a startup gate that refuses forward-auth mode unless an explicit trusted-proxy configuration is set, and document the NetworkPolicy boundary as a hard prerequisite for forward-auth deployments. Reject/strip the forwarded-identity headers on requests that do not arrive via the trusted path.
milestones: M1 Startup gate requiring trusted-proxy config in forward-auth mode; M2 strip/reject spoofable headers off the untrusted path; M3 document NetworkPolicy prerequisite in the deployment guide.

weakness: policy-manager evaluate/test handlers io.ReadAll the request body with no MaxBytesReader floor when the rate-limiter is disabled: the body-size cap is enforced by the rate-limit middleware, so disabling the rate limiter removes the request-body ceiling on the evaluate/test RPCs, leaving them open to an unbounded-allocation memory-exhaustion DoS (SC-5).
remediation: Wrap the evaluate/test handler bodies with http.MaxBytesReader at a hard floor independent of the rate-limit middleware, so the body ceiling holds even when rate limiting is off. Add a test posting an oversized body and asserting 413.
milestones: M1 MaxBytesReader floor on evaluate/test handlers; M2 oversized-body 413 test; M3 audit other ReadAll sites for the same gap.

weakness: SIEM forward backend pins a TLS 1.2 floor (vs TLS 1.3 elsewhere) and exposes an insecure-skip-verify opt-in with no production guard: the audit forward output's TLS config is inconsistent with the system-wide TLS 1.3 floor, and the skip-verify toggle can disable server-cert verification on the audit-shipping channel with nothing preventing its use in production (SC-8).
remediation: Make the forward-backend TLS floor configurable, default it to TLS 1.3 to match the rest of the system, and refuse insecure-skip-verify when running in a production profile (gate the toggle behind an explicit non-production flag). Add a test asserting the default floor and the production refusal.
milestones: M1 Configurable TLS floor default 1.3; M2 production-profile refusal of skip-verify; M3 test default + refusal paths.

weakness: Code-quality cleanups identified in independent review (SA-15 development-process hygiene; no direct exploit): (a) vestigial Manager.ctx/cancel fields are carried but unused; (b) the audit Context.Object field aliases the live request payload across the async flush boundary, risking a data race / mutation-after-handoff; (c) RecentDecisions accepts a negative limit and relies on a downstream clamp rather than validating at the boundary.
remediation: Cleanups: remove the vestigial Manager.ctx/cancel; deep-copy (or document the immutability contract of) the audit Context.Object before the async flush so the async path never aliases a mutable live payload; validate the RecentDecisions limit at the boundary instead of relying on a downstream clamp.
milestones: M1 Remove vestigial ctx/cancel; M2 deep-copy/immutability fix for audit Context.Object; M3 validate RecentDecisions limit at boundary.

weakness: Internal independent review (P12-WU-04) identified three security/correctness weaknesses that were REMEDIATED in the same cycle, recorded here for register completeness and closure traceability: (1) HIGH (SSRF/exfil) — request- and CRD-supplied Rego was compiled and executed with OPA's full default capability set (http.send, net.lookup_ip_addr, opa.runtime); (2) HIGH (DoS) — admission evaluation used context.Background() with no deadline against the apiserver's <=10s admission timeout; (3) MODERATE (DoS) — the policy-manager evaluate/test RPCs had no per-evaluation timeout. All three are CLOSED, not open.
remediation: REMEDIATED in commit 055a8c0 (P12-WU-04): (1) internal/policy/lib_loader.go builds a restricted OPA capability set (strips http.send/net.lookup_ip_addr/opa.runtime/rego.parse_module/trace) + StrictBuiltinErrors, applied at the only two rego.New sites (engine.go preparedQueryFor, policy_validation.go ValidateRuleRego) covering the admission engine, evaluate/test/validate RPCs, and the CRD reconciler; (2) controller.go derives a 2s context.WithTimeout from the admission request; (3) the policy-manager evaluate/test RPCs get a 5s bound. New tests prove http.send/net.lookup_ip_addr/opa.runtime rules are rejected and legitimate rules still compile.
milestones: M1 DONE: untrusted-Rego capability sandbox + StrictBuiltinErrors at both rego.New sites; M2 DONE: 2s admission eval deadline derived from the request context; M3 DONE: 5s evaluate/test RPC timeout — go build + all unit/pkg tests (incl new sandbox tests) + golangci-lint 0 + gosec 0.
status: Remediated (Closed 2026-06-02): all three findings fixed and verified before assembling the authorization package. Evidence: commit 055a8c0 (P12-WU-04) — internal/policy/lib_loader.go, internal/policy/engine.go, internal/policy/policy_validation.go (+_test.go), internal/admission/controller.go, internal/policymanager/evaluate_handler.go, internal/policymanager/test_handler.go.
